mara.activity: Wake, wash my face, brush my teeth, dress in comfortable clothes, and make sure the phone is not still beside the bed. I carry my reading glasses from the nightstand if I need them.
mara.intention: Start slowly and check the shape of the day before chores begin.

mara.activity: Make coffee and a quiet breakfast, carrying the mug and food to the dining table. I put the tea bag and small brass spoon on the kitchen sink-cabinet countertop for later.
mara.intention: Eat before starting the Saturday household work.

mara.activity: Change the bedding, carrying the used bed linen to the hamper and bringing the clean bed linen into place. I sort the laundry into workable loads and start one load if the machines are available.
mara.intention: Keep the usual Saturday reset without rushing.

mara.activity: Water the balcony plants, carrying the watering can out and back, then wash my hands and have a glass of water.
mara.intention: Finish the morning chores and get a little air.

mara.activity: Make a simple lunch, carry it to the dining table, and clear the dishes afterward. I leave the kitchen ready for the evening meal rather than beginning any elaborate cooking.
mara.intention: Have a proper break before the afternoon.

mara.activity: Read for a while in the living room, carrying the book and reading glasses from the bedroom. I leave the book face-down with its receipt marking the page when I stop.
mara.intention: Rest before doing any optional work.

mara.activity: Do a contained editing block at home, opening the laptop and taking the active manuscript from the canvas folder. I review a few pages only, save the file, and return the proof pages to the folder.
mara.intention: Maintain a little work rhythm without letting it take over the day.

mara.activity: Close the laptop, make tea, and take it to the living room. I tidy the current papers into the canvas folder and leave the tea bags and brass spoon on the kitchen counter rather than putting them away yet.
mara.intention: End work cleanly and shift into the evening.

mara.activity: Shower and dress for the evening meal, choosing comfortable but presentable clothes. I put away the laundry that is ready and leave the remaining sorting for tomorrow if necessary.
mara.intention: Get ready without turning preparation into another task list.

mara.activity: Set the dining table and prepare a small salad or other simple contribution to the meal, carrying plates, glasses, and cutlery from the kitchen. I keep the preparation light so Julian can manage his own cooking plans.
mara.intention: Make the shared meal welcoming while leaving Julian room to cook as he intends.

mara.activity: Share the evening meal with Julian and our friend. I listen closely, add precise observations when they occur to me, and help carry dishes or water as needed. When the unexpected outage interrupts the evening, I stop trying to monitor the schedule, use the available candle or flashlight, and sit with them through the unstructured pause.
mara.intention: Enjoy the break from routine and let the conversation continue without forcing it through the outage.

mara.activity: See our friend out, collect the most vulnerable dishes from the living room, and leave the rest safely grouped in the kitchen rather than attempting a full cleanup if the outage is still affecting things.
mara.intention: Restore enough order for the night without erasing the evening's ease.

mara.activity: Wash my face and brush my teeth, change into sleep clothes, and put my reading glasses on the nightstand by the bed.
mara.intention: Return to the usual bedtime routine after an unusual evening.

mara.activity: Put my phone on charge by the wardrobe, read a few pages in bed if the power has returned or use the flashlight briefly, then turn out the light and sleep.
mara.intention: End the day quietly and keep the phone out of reach overnight.

julian.activity: Wake slowly, take my temperature, drink water, and sit on the edge of the bed before getting up.
julian.intention: Check how I am feeling and start the day without overexerting myself.

julian.activity: Wash, brush my teeth, change into comfortable daytime clothes, and put my sleep clothes in the hamper.
julian.intention: Get ready while conserving energy.

julian.activity: Make weak tea and carry it with crackers and a little banana to the living-room sofa, then eat slowly.
julian.intention: Have a light breakfast and see whether my appetite and energy are returning.

julian.activity: Rest on the large sofa with my phone nearby, keeping museum notifications silenced.
julian.intention: Recover rather than repeat the usual Saturday errands.

julian.activity: Take my temperature again, take an ordinary dose of medicine after checking the label, and refill my water.
julian.intention: Manage the lingering illness responsibly.

julian.activity: Make a short list of the evening meal and check the kitchen supplies, clearing yesterday's plate and fork from beside the sink.
julian.intention: Prepare practically for the friend without committing to a complicated menu.

julian.activity: Eat a small lunch at the kitchen island and leave the dishes by the sink afterward.
julian.intention: Keep lunch simple and protect my energy for the evening.

julian.activity: Rest or sleep on the large sofa, with the phone on silent.
julian.intention: Take a proper recovery break before doing anything more active.

julian.activity: Make a brief, low-effort trip to collect a parcel and buy any missing meal item, then return home.
julian.intention: Handle only the essential errand rather than doing the full usual Saturday round.

julian.activity: Put the parcel and shopping away, wash my hands, and drink water.
julian.intention: Reset after going out and avoid bringing clutter into the evening.

julian.activity: Sit with my exhibition notes briefly, then stop before fatigue builds.
julian.intention: Do something recognisably mine while making today different from the usual long work session.

julian.activity: Prepare a simple evening meal, keeping the cooking oil and wooden spoon on the island while I work, and set out the dining table.
julian.intention: Host warmly without attempting an elaborate production.

julian.activity: Finish the meal, put food into serving dishes, fill the fridge with drinks, and put music on early.
julian.intention: Get the practical hosting details done while I still have energy.

julian.activity: Clear the dining table, bring the food and drinks out, and check the room before the friend arrives.
julian.intention: Make the shared space welcoming and easy to use.

julian.activity: Eat with the friend and make the conversation lively, carrying plates and glasses between the dining table and kitchen as needed.
julian.intention: Enjoy the break from routine and keep the evening buoyant.

julian.activity: When the unexpected outage interrupts the evening, turn off and check the kitchen appliances safely, find the flashlight, and reassure Mara and the friend.
julian.intention: Diagnose the immediate situation without taking unnecessary risks.

julian.activity: Settle into an unstructured, candlelit pause with the friend, talking and listening while the outage continues.
julian.intention: Let the enforced pause become part of the evening instead of trying to restore the schedule immediately.

julian.activity: See the friend out, gather the most perishable food, and leave the remaining dishes safely by the sink rather than attempting a full cleanup in the dark.
julian.intention: Close the visit sensibly while preserving energy.

julian.activity: Once the immediate inconvenience has passed, check the power and send one brief reassuring message if needed, then put my phone away.
julian.intention: Confirm that the household is safe and stop monitoring the outage.

julian.activity: Take a lukewarm shower, brush my teeth, and change into fresh comfortable clothes.
julian.intention: Wind down after hosting and avoid overdoing the evening.

julian.activity: Check my temperature, refill my water bottle, and put the phone on silent on the nightstand.
julian.intention: Make sure the illness has not worsened and prepare for sleep.

julian.activity: Get into bed and rest quietly, using tissues or water if needed.
julian.intention: Recover fully after the unusually social day.
